title: Light Sails Hit a Relativistic Speed Limit
hook: Laser-driven sails are our best idea for reaching another star. New work says relativity turns the light itself into drag once the sail passes roughly 75% of light speed.
key_points: A light sail accelerates by reflecting photons — momentum transfer with no fuel on board.
As the sail approaches light speed, the incoming light is redshifted and the push weakens.
The new twist: photons scattered off the sail can start acting as drag rather than thrust.
The turnover is estimated at around 75% of the speed of light.
That caps the cruise speed of laser-driven interstellar missions, lengthening travel times.
content_html: A light sail is the most credible interstellar propulsion scheme we have: leave the power plant at home, point an enormous laser at a gossamer mirror, and let photon momentum do the pushing for years on end. In principle the sail can coast up to a large fraction of light speed.
extra_html: The catch, according to NASA-reported work covered by ScienceDaily, is that relativity eventually turns the beam against you. Two effects compound: the faster you go, the more the incoming laser light is redshifted in your frame and the weaker its push — and, more surprisingly, light scattered off the sail can begin to remove momentum instead of adding it. The researchers put the crossover at roughly 75% of the speed of light, where scattering becomes an effective drag. That does not rule out interstellar sails, but it sets a practical ceiling on cruise speed, and so on how short a trip to the nearest stars could ever be.

related.title: Special Relativity, Gently
related.hook: Einstein started with one strange fact — light's speed is the same for everyone — and out fell that time itself can stretch.

related.title: E = mc²: Mass Is Energy
related.hook: The most famous equation in physics says mass and energy are the same thing. Because the speed of light squared is a colossal number, a tiny bit of mass holds a staggering amount of energy.

related.title: Is Light a Wave or a Particle?
related.hook: Light behaves like a wave in some experiments and like a stream of particles in others — and the surprising answer is that it's both.

related.title: We Might Already Be Overlooking Signs of Alien Life
related.hook: It's not just that we haven't found alien life — researchers warn we might be looking right at evidence of it and not recognizing it, because we mostly search for signs that look like Earth's own.

flashcards.prompt: How does a light sail accelerate without carrying fuel?
flashcards.back_html: Photons carry momentum. Reflecting a powerful laser beam off the sail transfers that momentum to the spacecraft, so the propellant stays behind on the ground.

flashcards.prompt: According to the study, what happens to a light sail near 75% of light speed?

choices.text: Scattered photons begin to act as drag, working against the thrust
The sail's mass becomes infinite and it stops instantly

flashcards.explanation_html: Relativistic effects mean light scattered off the sail can subtract momentum rather than add it, so beyond roughly 75% c the beam starts fighting the acceleration it created.
